newsitem.title: USA: Cold shuts two Colonial Pipeline links, no delays.
newsitem.headline: Cold shuts two Colonial Pipeline links, no delays.

text.p: Electrical outages caused by cold weather halted injections to the Colonial Pipeline at two points Monday, though there has been no reduction in line shipments, a pipeline spokesman said.

Injections from Port Arthur, TX and Lake Charles, LA. were halted early Monday due to power outages from ice that accompanied a winter storm. The injections will resume as soon as power is restored later Monday, the spokesman said.
The pipeline spokesman said it was unclear whether barrels from refineries at those points was scheduled to be shipped Monday, though no delays would occur even if there were.
"The outages just forced us to do upstream liftings earlier than normal," the spokesman said.

The arterial Colonial Pipeline extends from Houston to Linden, New Jersey, on the edge of New York Harbor and includes a 960,000 barrel per day (bpd) distillate line and a 1.2 million bpd gasoline line. The owners of the Pipeline include Amoco Corp, Atlantic Richfield Co, Petroleos de Venezuela SA's Citgo Petroleum Co, DuPont Co's Conoco Inc, Mobil Corp, Phillips Petroleum Co, Texaco Inc, Union Oil, of Unocal Corp, and Marathon Oil Co, a unit of USX-Marathon Group.
-- Matt Daily, New York Energy Desk, +1 212 859 1620
